Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Carlos (Verdigris Head of Platform), Priya (Cloud Architect), Liam (Security), Sofia (SRE), Benji (Purchasing)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: High-level discovery on private connectivity options for Redwood Private. Main topics: transit gateway vs peering, private endpoints, region constraints (DE/eu-central-1 requirement), egress restrictions, KMS/HSM integration, and timeline for pilot.
Topics: ingress/egress architecture, IP planning, latency expectations, dedicated vs hosted fit, compliance needs.
Action items: see metadata list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro — I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, and Jordan is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Carlos: Hi, Carlos here. Thanks. We have Priya and Liam as well — we'll probably point questions to them on network and security.
[00:19] Jordan (Redwood): Hey all. Quick agenda — understand Verdigris' current network topology, constraints for regions/data residency, and map that to Redwood Private deployment options. We'll surface the engineering tradeoffs for peering, transit, and private endpoints.
[00:31] Priya (Verdigris): Sounds good. Just to set expectations, Verdigris needs the inference plane in eu-central-1 for data residency — Germany — and we can't have model payloads traverse the public internet.
[00:40] Liam (Security): Also important: customer-managed KMS, per-request audit logs, and egress whitelist only to our internal telemetry and the KMS endpoints.
[00:49] Jordan: Got it. Couple quick clarifying q's — do you have a transit gateway already in prod that we can peer with, or is this more of a VPC-to-VPC peering primary pattern?
[00:59] Priya: We run a Transit Gateway in eu-central-1 that connects several VPCs; we prefer transit because it centralizes routing but we have strict route propagation rules.
[01:08] Maya: Good, that helps. For Redwood Private we can do either — we support deploying into customer VPCs with private endpoints, or you can use a peered VPC model where Redwood-managed endpoints appear as private IPs. There are latency and management tradeoffs.
[01:22] Carlos: Can you explain the difference in the context of our throughput needs? We expect spikes during batch scoring — potentially 500 conc reqs sustained for short bursts.
[01:34] Jordan: Sure. With VPC peering, traffic routes directly between your VPC and the Redwood VPC — low hop count, predictable latency. With Transit Gateway, you get better central control and simpler many-to-many topologies, but you need to consider route table scaling and cross-account attachment costs. Also the gw attachment can add a tiny ms depending on path.
[01:52] Priya: What about private endpoints? We heard about private endpoint DNS rewriting — how does that work with our split-horizon DNS?
[02:00] Jordan: We do provide private endpoints that resolve to private IPs in your VPC. Typically we publish an endpoint name you CNAME to an internal record or you can use Route53 inbound endpoints. We have seen customers use split-horizon to map model APIs to internal names. Sometimes the auto-generated cert names get a little messy — apologies if earlier docs miss those details.
[02:18] Liam: Certificate management — we want mTLS between our services and Redwood. Is mutual TLS supported on the private plane?
[02:25] Maya: Yes, mTLS can be negotiated. For Private deployments we can terminate at the customer side or at Redwood side depending on your certificate authority preferences. If you need mutual auth with your internal PKI, we can hand you the server cert and you can request client certs. Jordan can share specifics.
[02:38] Jordan: We'll send a cert flow diagram. One note — some customers misconfigure security groups and end up with asymmetric routing; watch the route tables and source/dest checks.
[02:47] Priya: Noted. How do we handle local egress filtering? Our policy blocks outbound except to certain FQDNs. The inference runtime calls home for telemetry and possibly model updates — can that be constrained?
[02:58] Jordan: Yes — telemetry and model artifact fetches can be routed to a customer-managed artifact proxy or to a narrow set of FQDNs. For strict egress, customers either host an internal cache or we allow access to a short allow-list. We'll provide an allow-list for the deployment.
[03:14] Carlos: About KMS — we run customer-managed KMS in our account, plus a separate HSM provider for key wrapping. Can Redwood integrate with external KMS/HSM for encryption-at-rest?
[03:25] Maya: Absolutely. For Private we support integrating with your KMS via IAM roles and endpoint policies. For HSM, we support key-wrap flows — Jordan, any notes on KMS connectors?
[03:33] Jordan: We'll need to add an endpoint to allow traffic to the KMS endpoint — if it's a service in your VPC that's straightforward. If it's a managed KMS with restricted endpoints, we have a pattern to call the KMS over VPC endpoints or through a customer proxy. There may be some latency impact but it's usually negligible for token key lookup.
[03:48] Sofia (SRE): Quick infra question — MTU and jumbo frames. Our internal VPCs use 9001 MTU for high throughput between colo and cloud. Any impact for the KV cache syncs?
[03:57] Jordan: Good callout. Most of our runtime paths can handle jumbo frames but you'll want to ensure your peering/Transit Gateway caps match. If packets are fragmented it can add latency. We'll surface recommended MTU settings for the bench.
[04:09] Priya: Are there IP planning constraints? We want to avoid overlapping CIDRs; we run a pretty saturated address space.
[04:15] Maya: We usually ask for a /27 or /28 per endpoint range — small but sufficient for NATing internal endpoints. If you've exhausted space we can do shared NATs but that complicates security.
[04:26] Carlos: How about multi-region failover? We want primary in eu-central-1 but failover to eu-west-1 if needed; data residency is a must — can failover be controlled so no PII leaves Germany except in DR mode with approvals?
[04:39] Jordan: We support region-routing policies. Typically you pin a model to a region and configure fallbacks. For strict residency, we can implement allow-only failover after an approval gate — that can be automated via console flags or manual ops.
[04:51] Liam: Audit logs — we need request-level logs for all inference calls for compliance. Are logs stored in our S3 with SSE-KMS?
[04:58] Maya: Yes, logs can be delivered to your S3 with SSE-KMS. We also provide a copy to Redwood's observability but you can opt out. We'll provide schema for logs and retention options.
[05:09] Benji (Purchasing): Timeline and cost — rough ballpark for a pilot? We're leaning towards a quarterly committed Dedicated if the numbers look good.
[05:18] Maya: For pilots we often do a 30-day reserved small pool or a hosted trial with dedicated capacity behind a private endpoint. I'll send pricing bands — ballpark depends on model size and peak tokens. For a committed Dedicated we'd propose a reserved pool with higher SLA.
[05:29] Priya: One more nutty question — does Redwood require any outbound connectivity for license checks or is everything local?
[05:35] Jordan: No third-party license check by default. Model weights can be hosted locally in your VPC, so no outbound for model fetches if you prefer. Some management plane features may call home but those are optional.
[05:46] Carlos: Great. Can we run a technical bench? We want a short 30-60 minute session: deploy a tiny model in our VPC, run latency p95 and throughput tests and capture egress patterns.
[05:55] Maya: Absolutely. Jordan will coordinate the bench. We'll need the CIDRs and a staging VPC for the attach.
[06:01] Jordan: I'll put together a bench checklist and share a small terraform snippet that attaches the endpoint and sample security group rules.
[06:08] Priya: We'll probably want to vet the terraform internally first. Expect to share CIDRs by Friday.
[06:14] Maya: Nice. Let's capture next steps — Maya to send docs and pricing, Jordan to prep bench checklist, Verdigris to share networking details. Any other questions?
[06:25] Liam: One last: SSO/SAML — we want RBAC integrated with our IdP for admin controls.
[06:30] Maya: Supported. We have SAML/SCIM provisioning for admin users. We'll include the SAML metadata in the pack.
[06:36] Sofia: Will you share the telemetry allow-list and a sample route table mapping?
[06:40] Jordan: Yes, both coming in the integration guide.
[06:44] Carlos: Thanks everyone — this was helpful.
[06:47] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the packet.
[06:50] End of call.
